title: [FEAT]: Document Generic OpenAI native tool-calling flag and warn when automatic agents fall back to UnTooled
body:
## Summary

Generic OpenAI endpoints that support native tool/function calling can silently fall back to `UnTooled` unless `PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_NATIVE_TOOL_CALLING` includes `generic-openai`.

This is documented on the general configuration page, but it is easy to miss from the Generic OpenAI setup flow. The current UX also makes this hard to diagnose because automatic agent mode may appear enabled while tool use still falls back to the prompt-based `UnTooled` path.

## Observed Behavior

On AnythingLLM `1.12.1` with:

```env
LLM_PROVIDER='generic-openai'
GENERIC_OPEN_AI_MODEL_PREF='cx/gpt-5.4-mini'
```

and no:

```env
PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_NATIVE_TOOL_CALLING="generic-openai"
```

logs show:

```text
Generic OpenAI supports native tool calling is DISABLED. Will use UnTooled instead.
Untooled.stream - will process this chat completion.
```

In this state:

- Workspace `chatMode='automatic'` does not invoke tools without `@agent`.
- Agent skills are attached and selected.
- Multi-step tools can behave unreliably because the system is using the prompt-based fallback.
- In one real case, Gmail repeatedly invoked `gmail-search` but never invoked `gmail-read-thread`.

After setting:

```env
PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_NATIVE_TOOL_CALLING="generic-openai"
```

and restarting, logs changed to:

```text
Generic OpenAI supports native tool calling is ENABLED.
Provider.stream (tooled) - will process this chat completion.
```

The same Gmail workflow then successfully invoked:

```text
gmail-get-inbox
gmail-read-thread
```

and automatic mode worked without `@agent`.

## UX Problem

The current behavior is technically documented, but it is not surfaced where users configure Generic OpenAI.

The Generic OpenAI setup page describes OpenAI-compatible endpoints, but does not clearly call out that native tool calling requires:

```env
PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_NATIVE_TOOL_CALLING="generic-openai"
```

The general configuration page also says:

```text
This setting only applies to local LLM providers.
```

but the listed providers include `Generic OpenAI`, `Groq`, `AWS Bedrock`, and `OpenRouter`, which are not necessarily local providers. That wording is confusing.

## Suggested Improvements

- Add a warning/note to the Generic OpenAI setup page:
  - If your endpoint supports native tools/function calling, set `PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_NATIVE_TOOL_CALLING="generic-openai"`.
  - Restart the container/service after changing it.
- In the UI, warn when:
  - Provider is `generic-openai`
  - Workspace chat mode is `automatic`
  - Agent skills are enabled
  - Native tool calling is not enabled
- Improve log wording to include the exact remediation:
  - `Set PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_NATIVE_TOOL_CALLING="generic-openai" to enable native tool calling for this provider.`
- Clarify the docs wording that this applies to provider integrations that cannot auto-detect tool support, not only local providers.

## Why This Matters

Without this flag, users can end up debugging model, proxy, connector, or network behavior when the real issue is that AnythingLLM is intentionally using `UnTooled`.

This particularly affects multi-step tools such as Gmail, where search/list tools may run but follow-up tools like `gmail-read-thread` may never be invoked.

title: [FEAT]: detect native tool support for Generic OpenAI-compatible endpoints before falling back to UnTooled
body:
## Summary

Generic OpenAI currently appears to require manual opt-in via:

```env
PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_NATIVE_TOOL_CALLING="generic-openai"
```

before AnythingLLM uses native tool calling. If the flag is absent, Generic OpenAI falls back to `UnTooled`.

It would be useful for AnythingLLM to detect or probe native tool support for OpenAI-compatible endpoints before falling back.

## Use Case

Many OpenAI-compatible routers/proxies expose model capability metadata or support standard `tools` parameters even though they are configured through AnythingLLM as `generic-openai`.

Example endpoint behavior:

```json
{
  "id": "cx/gpt-5.4-mini",
  "capabilities": {
    "tool_calling": true,
    "reasoning": true
  }
}
```

In this setup, the endpoint and selected model support tools, but AnythingLLM still uses `UnTooled` unless the operator manually sets the env flag.

## Observed Behavior

With AnythingLLM `1.12.1`:

```env
LLM_PROVIDER='generic-openai'
GENERIC_OPEN_AI_MODEL_PREF='cx/gpt-5.4-mini'
PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_NATIVE_TOOL_CALLING=<unset>
```

logs show:

```text
Generic OpenAI supports native tool calling is DISABLED. Will use UnTooled instead.
```

The endpoint's `/v1/models` response advertises `capabilities.tool_calling: true`, but AnythingLLM does not appear to use this metadata for Generic OpenAI capability detection.

After setting:

```env
PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_NATIVE_TOOL_CALLING="generic-openai"
```

logs show:

```text
Generic OpenAI supports native tool calling is ENABLED.
Provider.stream (tooled) - will process this chat completion.
```

and native tool calls work.

## Proposed Behavior

Before falling back to `UnTooled`, Generic OpenAI could attempt one or more of:

- Read `/v1/models` for the selected model and check common capability fields:
  - `capabilities.tool_calling`
  - `capabilities.tools`
  - `tool_calling`
  - `supports_tools`
- Optionally perform a small non-destructive tool-call probe against the configured model.
- Cache the detected capability per provider/base URL/model.
- Keep the env var as an explicit override:
  - env true: force native tool calling
  - env false/absent: auto-detect if possible
  - detected unsupported: fall back to `UnTooled`

## Safety / Compatibility

The current conservative behavior is understandable because not every OpenAI-compatible endpoint supports tools. The enhancement could preserve that safety by:

- Keeping `UnTooled` fallback when detection fails.
- Logging the detection result clearly.
- Allowing operators to force-enable or force-disable via env.
- Avoiding probes unless explicitly enabled, if runtime probes are considered too invasive.

## Why This Matters

Without auto-detection, users of OpenAI-compatible routers can end up with degraded agent behavior even when their endpoint and model support native tools.

In one real case, this caused Gmail agent behavior where:

- `gmail-search` was invoked repeatedly.
- `gmail-read-thread` was never invoked.
- The agent claimed it could not access/read Gmail message bodies.
- Setting `PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_NATIVE_TOOL_CALLING="generic-openai"` fixed the issue.

This makes the current fallback difficult to diagnose and can look like a connector, network, or model refusal issue rather than a provider capability configuration issue.

title: [FEAT]: Heartbeat for agent chats
body:
### What would you like to see?

When in an agent chat session it is possible that during work on the server the websocket connection could go a very long time between messages.

For example, consider a connection where the model needs to call some very computationally heavy tool or maybe the model itself needs time for processing. This means the user could see the initial response from the socket then wait a long time before the next packet comes in.

For some tunnels like ngrok or zrok you cannot control the TTL of the tunnel and it can close after some period of time with no traffic (eg: 60s).

If anythingllm sent a simple `alive` packet to the frontend and did nothing with it we could keep the tunnel open with no side effects.

This hearbeat **must** still respect the total socket TTL or else they will never close.

title: OpenAI and Anthropic provider calls should use explicit timeouts and retry/backoff
body:
### What would you like to see?

```md
Support/document OpenAI-compatible gateway base URLs for production reliability
```

**Issue body**

````md
## Question

Would maintainers be open to a small PR that documents or improves support for OpenAI-compatible gateway base URLs?

Some production users route LLM calls through a gateway layer so they can manage:

- retries
- fallback routing
- request tracking
- provider timeout handling
- debugging failed provider calls

For example, an OpenAI-compatible client can usually point at a gateway by changing only the API key and base URL:

```ts
import OpenAI from "openai";

const openai = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: process.env.BADGR_API_KEY,
  baseURL: "https://api.aibadgr.com/v1",
});
````

## Why I'm asking

I noticed a few LLM provider paths where reliability behavior may currently depend on the underlying provider/client defaults:

* `server/utils/AiProviders/openAi/index.js`

  * OpenAI requests appear to be issued directly without an explicit timeout or abort budget
  * completion calls appear to rely on direct provider errors without a shared retry/backoff policy
  * error rethrows may drop useful provider metadata such as status code, headers, request IDs, or retry hints

* `server/utils/AiProviders/anthropic/index.js`

  * Anthropic requests appear to run without an explicit timeout or abort budget
  * transient `429` / `5xx` provider errors may fail immediately
  * one error path appears to return the error object as `textResponse`, which could be treated like a successful model response upstream

* `server/utils/chats/apiChatHandler.js`

  * chat execution appears to use one resolved provider per request without an optional runtime fallback chain if that provider is unavailable

* `server/utils/helpers/chat/LLMPerformanceMonitor.js`

  * performance tracking appears to capture duration/token metrics, but not full upstream failure taxonomy such as provider status, retry count, fallback step, timeout reason, or request correlation ID

These may already be handled elsewhere, so I wanted to ask before opening a larger PR.

## Possible small PR options

Happy to follow whatever maintainers prefer:

1. a small docs PR showing how to configure an OpenAI-compatible gateway base URL
2. a small config improvement for custom OpenAI-compatible base URLs
3. a small timeout/retry improvement in one provider path
4. improved structured error metadata for provider failures
5. no change, if this is outside the project scope

The goal would be optional production reliability support without changing default behavior.

title: Ollama provider: "Auto-detect from model" label is misleading - value is hard-capped at 16384 tokens regardless of model's actual context
body:
### How are you running AnythingLLM?
AnythingLLM desktop app (Linux AppImage, current release)

### What happened?

The "Model Context Window" setting in the Ollama LLM provider shows "Auto-detect from model" by default. Users running larger-context models (e.g. `gpt-oss:20b`, native 131072) reasonably expect the detected value to be used - but it is silently capped at 16384.

This is the cap (intentional, per the code comment) at [`server/utils/AiProviders/ollama/index.js:199`](https://github.com/Mintplex-Labs/anything-llm/blob/master/server/utils/AiProviders/ollama/index.js#L199):

```js
// Cap the context window limit to 16,384 tokens if the model supports more than that and no value is specified by the user.
// This prevents super-large context windows from being used if the user does not specify a value
// as well as also having smaller context windows use the full context window limit.
return Math.min(systemDefinedLimit, 16384);
```

The cap itself is reasonable as a safety default - large KV caches can OOM users on smaller GPUs. The issue is that the **UI label doesn't communicate this behavior**. A user reading "Auto-detect from model" is not told that the auto-detection result is clamped to 16k.

### Concrete impact

Running `gpt-oss:20b` on Ollama with adequate VRAM (16 GB):

- `cacheContextWindows()` correctly detects 131072 from `/api/show` (`gptoss.context_length: 131072`)
- `promptWindowLimit()` returns `min(131072, 16384) = 16384`
- AnythingLLM sends `num_ctx: 16384` to Ollama

Additional downstream effect: when this AnythingLLM workspace shares an Ollama instance with another client (e.g. Claude Code) that uses the server default `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH`, every switch triggers Ollama to tear down and reload the runner because `num_ctx` is part of the runner's load-option key. On a Radeon VII this reload is ~30s per switch.

### Related issues

- #4583 - same model (`gpt-oss:20b`), same surface symptom, closed without root-cause identification. The user reported that even manually setting 128000 didn't change behavior; that may be a separate paperclip code path, but the underlying auto-detect cap matches what we observed.
- #4909 - the refactor PR that introduced the 16384 cap.

### Suggested fixes (any one of these would address the UX concern)

1. **Rename the UI option** - e.g. `Auto-detect (capped at 16k unless overridden)` - so the cap is visible from the UI label alone.
2. **Add a tooltip** explaining the cap and how to override.
3. **Surface the effective context value** in the LLM settings view (currently only available via a log line at provider load).
4. **Use the model's full detected context when sufficient VRAM is available** - feasible only if AnythingLLM can probe free VRAM, which is hard cross-platform, so probably skip this one.

I'd happily contribute a PR for option 1 or 2 if maintainers agree on the direction.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install Ollama; `ollama pull gpt-oss:20b`
2. In AnythingLLM, set LLM provider to Ollama, model `gpt-oss:20b`
3. Leave "Model Context Window" at default ("Auto-detect from model")
4. Send any prompt
5. Observe (e.g. via `OLLAMA_DEBUG_LOG_REQUESTS=true` on the Ollama server) that AnythingLLM sends `num_ctx: 16384` instead of 131072.

title: [FEAT]: Rework summarize tool
body:
### What would you like to see?

The summarize tool tends to lock up on small local models. We should remove langchain from this tool and do it in a simpler way where we chunk it and prompt the user after 3 chunks if they would like to continue. This will greatly improve the UX on smaller context window models.


When entering the summary loop:
- Get model context window (if needed again)
- Chunk the content to be 45% of context window of the model
- Send these chunks one at a time asking ONLY for the key points of this section
- Include the previous points in the next loop iteration, but previous points should not make up more than 5% of the window. If it exceeds that truncate the content from the start so that the details of the last chunk summary are appended to the next chunk in case we split in the middle of a piece of content.
- After 3 chunk loops, before doing chunk 4 if it exists - ask the user if it is OK to continue or if it should skip
- We can count details/concepts from non-empty newlines?

User Experience:
- I ask model to do some deep research in an on-demand chat (regular chat)
- Model finds some VERY verbose website or content
- Event sent to UI that this content is very long and will need to be summarized
- chunk logic applied to content -> start processing chunk by chunk
- if chunks <4 model finishes and returns its bullet list from the tool
- if more:
    - Model returns to user a `requestToolApproval` event asking if it is okay to continue
    - Inform the user via this action "There are x more pieces of content I can summarize - Continue?"
    - If they say yes -> continue again without asking through the whole document
    - If they deny -> return the content as it is in its current state.

This should prevent this tool from needlessly locking up the whole UI because it comes across some large content.

title: SearXNG search query is double encoded
body:
SearXNG searches seem to be double encoding the query.

Example query:

```text
Colossus and the Crab ending D.F. Jones book 3 plot summary
```

gets sent as:

```text
/search?q=Colossus%2520and%2520the%2520Crab%2520ending%2520D.F.%2520Jones%2520book%25203%2520plot%2520summary&format=json
```

So SearXNG receives `Colossus%20and%20...` as the query instead of normal text.

Looks like this line is the cause:

```js
searchURL.searchParams.append("q", encodeURIComponent(query));
```

`URLSearchParams` already handles encoding, so passing `query` directly fixes it:

```js
searchURL.searchParams.append("q", query);
```

I monkeypatched this locally and it resolves the issue, but I'd rather not carry that patch in my deployment.

title: Embed widgets answer requests from any origin by default (no deny-by-default for empty allowlist_domains)
body:
### What happened?

When a chat embed is created without `allowlist_domains`, the value defaults to `null`. In `server/models/embedConfig.js`, `parseAllowedHosts()` returns `null` for an empty/missing allowlist, and in `server/utils/middleware/embedMiddleware.js` (`canRespond`) the origin check is **skipped** when `allowedHosts === null`:

```js
const allowedHosts = EmbedConfig.parseAllowedHosts(embed);
if (allowedHosts !== null && !allowedHosts.includes(host)) { /* reject */ }
```

So an embed with no allowlist answers `/api/embed/{uuid}/stream-chat` from **any** origin. An operator who enables an embed for a single page unknowingly exposes that workspace's content to requests from every origin, and there's no warning at creation time and no way to make 'no allowlist' mean deny-all.

To be clear: public embeds are intentional and auth-less by design - this is **not** a request to require authentication. It's that the *secure default* and *operator awareness* are missing.

### Proposed solution (additive, non-breaking)

1. An opt-in server flag `EMBED_REQUIRE_ALLOWLIST=true` that makes the embed middleware reject requests to an embed whose allowlist is empty/null (deny-by-default). Unset preserves today's behavior.
2. A creation-time `console.warn` when an embed is created with no allowlist.
3. An `.env.example` entry documenting the flag.

I've opened a small PR implementing exactly this.

### Disclosure

This was surfaced while testing a self-hosted AnythingLLM instance with an automated multi-tenant-isolation checker ([Sectum AI](https://github.com/sectum-ai/sectum-ai)); this report was drafted with AI assistance.

title: [BUG]: Linux AppImage 1.13.0 reports version 1.12.1 in UI due to stale backend bundle
body:
### Describe the bug
The latest Linux AppImage for version 1.13.0 hosted on the CDN (`https://cdn.anythingllm.com/latest/AnythingLLMDesktop.AppImage`) incorrectly reports its version as `1.12.1` in the UI.

Despite the AppImage being the correct 1.13.0 build (matching the expected CDN file size), the bundled backend inside the AppImage still contains the hardcoded string `"version":"1.12.1"`. Because the frontend queries `/api/utils/metrics` to get the version number, the UI displays `1.12.1` to the user, making them think the app has failed to update.

### To Reproduce
1. Download the latest Linux AppImage using the official script (`curl -fsSL https://cdn.anythingllm.com/latest/installer.sh | sh`)
2. Open the AnythingLLM Desktop App.
3. Observe the version number in the UI, which says `1.12.1` instead of `1.13.0`.

### Expected behavior
The UI should correctly display `1.13.0`.

### Technical Details
If you extract the AppImage (`./AnythingLLMDesktop.AppImage --appimage-extract`), you can observe the mismatch:
- `squashfs-root/resources/app.asar` contains `package.json` with `"version": "1.13.0"`
- However, the bundled backend code (e.g. `squashfs-root/resources/backend/jobs/sync-watched-documents.js`) has `name:"anything-llm",version:"1.12.1"` hardcoded in the minified bundle.

This suggests that during the Linux AppImage build process for 1.13.0, the backend was bundled (via `combineModules.mjs`) using a stale cache or before `server/package.json` was properly bumped to 1.13.0.

title: fix(nuxt-port): clearAllChats uses magic -1 sentinel and optimistic clear
body:
## Summary

\`nuxt-frontend/core/application/useWorkspaceChats.ts\` - \`clearAllChats()\` calls \`api.deleteChat(-1)\` where \`-1\` is a magic sentinel meaning "delete all". Two problems:

1. **Leaky abstraction** - \`-1\` is an upstream API implementation detail bleeding into the application layer composable. A dedicated \`clearAllChats()\` port method would be more semantically honest and easier to mock in tests.
2. **Optimistic clear before confirmation** - the composable clears local state before the API call confirms success for all records. A partial server failure leaves the UI showing an empty list when records still exist.

## Fix

- Add a \`clearAllChats(): Promise<{ error: string | null }>\` method to \`WorkspaceChatsApiPort\`
- Implement it in the infrastructure adapter (maps to the same \`DELETE /api/system/workspace-chats/-1\` endpoint)
- Update \`clearAllChats()\` in \`useWorkspaceChats\` to call the port method and only clear local state on confirmed success

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] \`WorkspaceChatsApiPort\` has a \`clearAllChats()\` method
- [ ] \`useWorkspaceChats.clearAllChats()\` clears local state only after the API confirms success
- [ ] No \`deleteChat(-1)\` in application layer code
- [ ] Tests cover the partial-failure case (API returns error, local state preserved)

```
[workspace system prompt]
```

```
[workspace system prompt]
```

title: [BUG]: Scheduled jobs do not pass workspace context to EphemeralAgentHandler, breaking model router resolution
body:
### How are you running AnythingLLM?

Local development

### What happened?

Scheduled jobs currently instantiate EphemeralAgentHandler without a workspace. This works for direct provider configurations, but it causes problems when the system or scheduled-job execution path relies on anythingllm-router.

EphemeralAgentHandler already supports workspace-aware provider fallback and model-router resolution, but without a workspace it cannot reliably gather routing context, resolve workspace/router settings, or build the same route context used by normal chat and agent flows. As a result, scheduled jobs may fail, fall back incorrectly, or ignore the configured model router.

A minimal fix is to load/create the existing Scheduled Jobs workspace in server/jobs/run-scheduled-job.js and pass it into EphemeralAgentHandler, matching how scheduled job runs are later continued in a thread.

I implemented the above minimal fix myself, but only did quick manual tests to ensure it works.

Expected behavior
Scheduled jobs should use the configured model router when LLM_PROVIDER=anythingllm-router or when the scheduled jobs workspace is configured to use the router.

Actual behavior
Scheduled jobs run through EphemeralAgentHandler without workspace context, so router-backed execution does not receive the workspace data required for proper route resolution.

Additional note
Because scheduled jobs are currently global rather than workspace-scoped, the first-pass fix can use the existing synthetic scheduled-jobs workspace. A broader follow-up could consider making scheduled jobs explicitly workspace-scoped or giving each job/run an isolated routing scope to avoid shared sticky-route cache behavior.

### What would you like to see?

**Current Status:**
AnythingLLM currently has three roles: Admin (unrestricted access), Manager (can manage all workspaces, create accounts, etc.), and Default (can only use the system, cannot upload documents).

Among these three roles, the Manager role is somewhat redundant. While it can manage workspaces, it also has the ability to operate on workspaces created by other users, including deleting them. This overlaps partially with the Admin role and grants excessively high privileges.
**Recommendations:**
The Manager's permissions should be restricted to creating new workspaces and maintaining only the ones they have created. They should not be allowed to view or operate on workspaces created by other accounts. This ensures basic isolation and prevents the risk of accidental or malicious operations.
After clicking into a workspace, users should only see the documents belonging to their own workspace; the global file list in the left sidebar should not be visible.

title: [BUG]: Docs inconsistency: `ANYTHING_LLM_INSTALL_DIR` cannot be used with root-owned paths like `/opt`
body:
### How are you running AnythingLLM?

AnythingLLM desktop app

### What happened?

**Environment**
- OS: Ubuntu Studio 26.04, KDE 6.6.4 / Wayland
- Architecture: x64
- AnythingLLM version: 1.14.1

**What the docs say**

The Linux installation page states:

> "If you wish to install to a different location, set the `ANYTHING_LLM_INSTALL_DIR` environment variable before running the installer."

**What actually happens**

Running the installer with `sudo` in order to write to a root-owned directory (e.g. `/opt/anythingllm`) is blocked by the script itself:

```
$ sudo ANYTHING_LLM_INSTALL_DIR=/opt/anythingllm ./installer.sh
This script should not be run as root. Please run it as a regular user.
```

This means `ANYTHING_LLM_INSTALL_DIR` is effectively only usable for paths the current user already owns. Any standard system-wide install location (`/opt`, `/usr/local`, etc.) is unreachable.

**Workaround**

Run the installer normally (installs to `$HOME`), then manually move the AppImage with `sudo mv`:

```bash
./installer.sh
sudo mv ~/AnythingLLMDesktop.AppImage /opt/anythingllm/AnythingLLMDesktop.AppImage
```

**Suggested fix**

Either:
- Have the script use `sudo` internally only for the specific write step when the target directory requires elevated permissions, or
- Update the docs to clarify that `ANYTHING_LLM_INSTALL_DIR` only works for user-writable paths.

The current docs imply full flexibility over install location, which is misleading for users who prefer a system-wide install.

title: [FEAT]: Add native Google Vertex AI provider (service-account / ADC auth)
body:
### What would you like to see?

There's currently no way to use Google Vertex AI as an LLM provider without misusing the Generic OpenAI connector, and that workaround is structurally broken for Vertex.

Vertex's OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`{region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/.../endpoints/openapi`) authenticates with a short-lived OAuth access token (`credentials.token`) that expires after ~1 hour by default. The Generic OpenAI connector only accepts a static, paste-once API key, so even a successful connection dies ~60 minutes later with no way to refresh. The alternative - Vertex AI Express API keys - fails too, because the underlying SDK call routes to AI Studio URLs (`generativelanguage.googleapis.com`) instead of Vertex endpoints unless the Vertex flag is explicitly set.

Net result: Vertex is effectively unsupported, and the only working path is running a local proxy (e.g. LiteLLM) to hold the service-account JSON and handle token refresh - a lot to ask of non-technical users.

title: [INTEGRATION]: Add Valkey as a vector database provider
body:
## New Integration Proposal - Vector DB provider

Following the New Integration Proposal template.

**Provider Name:** Valkey (with the `valkey-search` module)

**Official Website URL:** https://valkey.io

**API Documentation URL:** https://valkey.io/topics/search/ and the official Node client `@valkey/valkey-glide` (https://github.com/valkey-io/valkey-glide)

**Privacy Policy URL:** Self-hosted/open-source - data never leaves the operator's own Valkey instance. Linux Foundation project: https://valkey.io (governance under https://lfprojects.org).

**Proof of Active User Base & Demand:** Valkey is a Linux Foundation project created in 2024 as the community fork of Redis after its license change, backed by AWS, Google Cloud, Oracle, Ericsson, and others. The core repo `valkey-io/valkey` has 20k+ GitHub stars, ships in major Linux distributions, and is offered as a managed service by multiple cloud providers. The `valkey-search` module adds HNSW vector similarity search. This comfortably clears the "1,000 stars on core open-source repo" footprint bar and has 90+ days of stable, publicly accessible production availability.

**Native Models Discovery:** N/A for a vector database (the `/v1/models` question applies to LLM providers).

**Technical Compatibility Layer:** This is not an OpenAI-compatible LLM connector and cannot be served by the Generic OpenAI connector - it is a distinct vector store. It requires custom orchestration via the official `@valkey/valkey-glide` SDK and the `valkey-search` module commands (`FT.CREATE` / `FT.SEARCH`, HNSW, COSINE), so it warrants a dedicated `VectorDatabase` provider alongside LanceDB, PGVector, Qdrant, Milvus, etc.

### What would you like to see?

AnythingLLM ships ten vector database providers today, selected via `VECTOR_DB` and resolved through `getVectorDbClass()`, with every provider extending the shared `VectorDatabase` base class. Valkey is not currently an option, so teams already running Valkey (for caching, queues, or as a primary datastore) must stand up a separate dedicated vector database purely for AnythingLLM's RAG layer.

This proposes adding Valkey as a native, first-class vector database provider - purely additive, with default behavior unchanged and Valkey used only when an operator sets `VECTOR_DB=valkey`.

Proposed shape (mirrors the existing PGVector/Qdrant providers):
- New `Valkey` provider at `server/utils/vectorDbProviders/valkey/index.js` extending `VectorDatabase`, registered as `case "valkey"` in `server/utils/helpers/index.js`.
- Official `@valkey/valkey-glide` client (server only, opt-in dependency); `valkey-search` module via the `valkey/valkey-bundle` image for vector ops.
- One `valkey-search` index per workspace/namespace (`allm_idx_{namespace}` over `allm:{namespace}:` hash keys) for clean isolation, counting, and deletion.
- HNSW + COSINE; KNN `FT.SEARCH`; FLOAT32 embeddings stored alongside text + metadata.
- Full capability parity with existing providers: add/delete document, delete-namespace, reset, similarity search with threshold + topN, `filterIdentifiers` exclusion, the vector cache path, namespace stats, optional TLS/auth, configurable request timeout.
- Settings plumbing in `updateENV.js` + `systemSettings.js`, env examples, a commented opt-in `docker-compose` service, and unit + live integration tests.

Happy to align on scope/conventions before opening a PR. Thanks for considering it!

body:
### Provider Name
Ofox

### Official Website URL
https://ofox.ai

### API Documentation URL
https://ofox.ai/docs

### Privacy Policy URL
https://ofox.ai/privacy

### Proof of Active User Base & Demand
Ofox has been operating a public, stable production API for ~6 months - well past the 90-day operational-longevity threshold in the vetting criteria. It serves 100+ models across providers; `GET /v1/models` currently returns 110 live models for dynamic discovery.

### Native Models Discovery
Yes - Ofox exposes a standard `GET /v1/models` endpoint for dynamic model enumeration.

### Technical Compatibility Layer
This provider is NOT (purely) OpenAI-compatible and offers capabilities the Generic OpenAI connector cannot reach - details below.

### Why a dedicated integration (beyond the Generic OpenAI connector)

**A. Aggregation + native model discovery (concrete).** One key gives access to 100+ models across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, Qwen, MiniMax, Zhipu, Moonshot and more, at each provider's official list price (no markup). `GET /v1/models` returns the full catalog, so AnythingLLM could populate and refresh the model dropdown automatically - which the manual base-URL Generic connector cannot do.

**B. Three native protocols on one key (architectural).** Ofox natively exposes not only the OpenAI-compatible surface (`/v1`) but also the **Anthropic-native** (`/anthropic`) and **Gemini-native** (`/gemini`) APIs under the same key. The Generic OpenAI connector can only reach the `/v1` surface, so protocol-native features (e.g. Anthropic `cache_control` prompt caching) are lost through a generic wrapper.

If this is of interest, I'm happy to open a PR following the existing aggregator pattern (e.g. `cometapi`) - a `/v1/models`-backed model cache, no `modelMap` bloat.

title: [BUG]: open-computer setup fails on Windows x64 (WHPX): blank display, VP exit code 4, ISO not attached, provision and build broken
body:
### How are you running AnythingLLM?

Local development

### What happened?

I tried to set up the `open-computer` project on Windows x64 with WHPX
acceleration using the bundled Windows QEMU binaries. Following the Quick Start
and DEVELOPMENT.md, `open-computer base install` opens a VM whose VNC display
stays blank ("Guest has not initialized the display (yet)"), so the Debian
installer can never be reached, and the rest of the flow (provision, build,
create agent) cannot complete.

After digging in, there are several separate Windows x64 problems in the CLI
(`open-computer/cli/src`). Each one independently blocks the setup:

1. EFI vars pflash is wrong. `base install` and `buildQemuArgs` copy the OVMF
   CODE firmware (`edk2-x86_64-code.fd`) into the writable vars file
   (`efi-vars.fd`) instead of the VARS template (`edk2-i386-vars.fd`). With no
   real variable store, OVMF never POSTs and the screen is blank. This is the
   main cause of the blank display.

2. Installer ISO is never attached. `base install` validates that the ISO
   exists but `buildQemuArgs` never adds a CD-ROM drive, so even once firmware
   boots there is no installer media.

3. WHPX crashes with `-cpu host`. On a recent AMD CPU (Ryzen 5 7600, Zen 4),
   `-cpu host` exposes APX/MPX features that WHPX rejects with
   "WHPX: Unexpected VP exit code 4" and QEMU exits.

4. Display adapter is not visible under OVMF on Windows. The build uses
   `virtio-gpu-pci`, which OVMF does not render to over VNC on the bundled
   Windows QEMU build, so nothing shows even after the vars fix.

5. No display backend on Windows. The bundled QEMU build reports only
   `-display none` (no gtk), but the gui path passes `-display gtk`, and the
   `-vnc` option is never actually added to the QEMU args.

6. Monitor socket cleanup fails. `fs.rmSync` on the AF_UNIX monitor socket
   throws EACCES on Windows, so `base kill` / `down` / `compact` crash.

7. `base install` calls a bare `qemu-img` (not the bundled binary), which is
   not on PATH.

8. Provisioning cannot enter the root password. `base provision` runs
   `su -c /tmp/provision.sh` over an ssh session with no PTY, so `su` cannot
   read the password.

9. Prod build uses the wrong bash. `open-computer build` runs
   `services/build.sh` with a bare `bash`, which on Windows resolves to the
   WSL launcher that does not have the Windows Node toolchain on PATH.

Expected: `open-computer base install` boots the Debian installer over VNC,
`base provision` and `build` complete, and `create <name>` starts an agent
that serves the UI on localhost:9800.

Environment:
- OS: Windows 11 (x64), AMD Ryzen 5 7600, WHPX enabled
- QEMU: bundled `master/qemu/qemu-win-x64.7z` (QEMU 11.0.1), accel whpx
- Node: v23, Debian 13.5.0 amd64 netinst guest

I have working fixes for all of the above and will open a pull request that
references this issue.

### Are there known steps to reproduce?

1. On Windows x64, unzip `master/qemu/qemu-win-x64.7z` and fetch the Debian
   13.5 amd64 ISO into `master/iso`.
2. Build the CLI (`cd cli && npm install && npx tsc --noEmit && npx esbuild
   src/index.ts --bundle --platform=node --target=node22 --outfile=dist/open-computer`).
3. Run `open-computer base install` and connect a VNC viewer to the install
   display. The screen stays blank ("Guest has not initialized the display").
4. Even after correcting the EFI vars, `-cpu host` under WHPX exits with
   "Unexpected VP exit code 4", and the installer ISO is not attached.

### LLM Provider & Model (if applicable)

LM Studio (OpenAI compatible endpoint). Not relevant to these platform bugs.

N/A

title: [BUG]: Magic Echo On-Screen Awareness for Generic OpenAI Connections
body:
### Bug Description

**This is a follow-up to #5984, which was closed as "completed" but the underlying backend error persists.**

In #5984, the maintainer suggested adding `PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_VISION="generic-openai"` to the desktop `.env` as a workaround for llama.cpp not returning model capabilities. While this workaround **does** make the UI show "On-Screen Awareness" as enabled, it **does not** fix the actual backend error that causes Magic Echo's smart transcription to fail.

The real error remains:

```
This smart transcription failed and fell back to raw transcription instead: i?.getModelCapabilities(...).then is not a function
```

This indicates that somewhere in the Magic Echo / On-Screen Awareness pipeline, the code expects `getModelCapabilities()` to return a Promise (so it can call `.then()` on it), but for the **llama.cpp (generic-openai) provider**, it returns a non-Promise value (likely `undefined` or a plain object). The `.env` workaround only populates the capability flags statically; it does not fix the fact that the calling code assumes a Promise-based API that this provider does not implement.

### Environment

- **AnythingLLM Desktop Version:** v1.15.0 (Windows)
- **Provider:** llama.cpp (via Generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
- **Model:** Gemma 4 12B (vision-capable, confirmed working for image input in main chat)
- **llama.cpp launch flags:** `llama-server.exe` with `--mmproj` (vision projector) and `--jinja` chat template

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure AnythingLLM Desktop to use a local llama.cpp server with a vision-capable model.
2. Add `PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_VISION="generic-openai"` to the `.env` file (the workaround from #5984).
3. Restart AnythingLLM.
4. Enable **Magic Echo** and **On-Screen Awareness**.
5. Observe that the toggle now appears active in the UI.
6. Attempt to use Magic Echo dictation with On-Screen Awareness.
7. **Result:** The smart transcription fails with the error `i?.getModelCapabilities(...).then is not a function` and falls back to raw transcription.

### Expected Behavior

Magic Echo should successfully call `getModelCapabilities()` (or handle a non-Promise return value) and proceed to send the screenshot context to the llama.cpp endpoint for smart transcription.

### Actual Behavior

The backend throws a TypeError because `.then()` is called on a non-Promise value, causing the entire smart transcription flow to abort and fall back to raw transcription.

### Screenshots / Logs

- **UI after workaround:** On-Screen Awareness appears enabled (from #5984).
- **Actual failure:** `This smart transcription failed and fell back to raw transcription instead: i?.getModelCapabilities(...).then is not a function`

*(Note: The `Assistant response prefill is incompatible with enable_thinking` errors seen in llama.cpp logs are a downstream side-effect of the failed request and should be disregarded for the purposes of this bug.)*

### Additional Context

- The same model works perfectly for vision tasks in the main AnythingLLM chat interface.
- The issue is **not** that llama.cpp lacks vision support; the issue is that the Magic Echo code path assumes `getModelCapabilities()` returns a Promise, which is not true for the generic-openai provider.
- The `.env` workaround from #5984 is therefore an incomplete fix - it patches the capability *detection*, but not the capability *consumption* code path.

### Suggested Fix

The code calling `getModelCapabilities()` in the Magic Echo pipeline should either:
1. Wrap the call in `Promise.resolve()` to normalize the return value, or
2. Check if the result is a Promise before calling `.then()`.

---

**Reference:** Issue #5984 (closed) - the workaround provided there does not resolve this backend TypeError.

## The problem

Currently, the GenericOpenAi provider (and #generateContent helper) assumes that all API attachments are images. When sending audio files via the API, AnythingLLM automatically wraps them in an image_url block along with the full data:audio/...;base64, prefix.

When using OpenAI-compatible backends that support audio (such as llama.cpp or native multimodal audio endpoints), this causes two issues:

1. Backends reject the request with 500 Invalid uri format because audio/... URIs are invalid inside an image_url block.
2. OpenAI's standardized schema for multimodal audio expects type: "input_audio" with a raw base64 string (without the data:audio/...;base64, Data URI prefix) and a format key (e.g., mp3, wav).

## The solution

Update the #generateContent method in /server/utils/AiProviders/genericOpenAi/index.js to inspect the MIME type of incoming attachments.

If an attachment's MIME type starts with audio/:

1. It should format the content object as type: "input_audio".
2. It should extract the raw base64 string by stripping the Data URI prefix (data:audio/...;base64,).
3. It should include the audio format (e.g., format: "mp3").

Thank you very much for your work!

title: Eden AI integration: partnership inquiry for a first class EU provider
body:
Hi Mintplex Labs team,

I am Victor from Eden AI. First, thanks for AnythingLLM, it is genuinely great to use.

I read your Criteria for New LLM Providers carefully, including the OpenAI-Compatibility Rule and the Strategic Partnership Exception, so I want to be upfront rather than open a standard integration PR.

Being honest on the technical side: Eden AI is OpenAI compatible (standard /v3/chat/completions and /models, bearer auth), so it already works today through your Generic OpenAI connector, with base URL https://api.edenai.run/v3 and an EDENAI_API_KEY. Under your rule that means we would not qualify for a dedicated integration as an unsolicited contribution, and I do not want to waste your review time.

So I am reaching out under your Strategic Partnership Exception instead. We are the Eden AI team, not a random third party, and we would be glad to build and maintain a first class integration for the long run.

Why a dedicated provider could be worth it over the generic connector:
- Eden AI is a European company, and that is the main point for EU teams: EU data residency (an EU endpoint at https://api.eu.edenai.run/v3), zero data retention, a DPA, and SOC 2 and ISO 27001. A dedicated provider lets us default to the EU endpoint and surface these guarantees in the UI, which the generic connector cannot.
- One key reaches models from many providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, Cohere and more) with vendor prefixed ids like openai/gpt-4o-mini, and we expose a models endpoint so the dropdown can populate on its own.
- We would own the maintenance, so this would not be a one time contribution that you inherit.

On market viability: Eden AI has been running a public and stable production API for well over 90 days (years in fact) as an established company, so this is not an early stage launch.

Reference links:
- Website: https://www.edenai.co
- API docs: https://www.edenai.co/docs
- Privacy policy: https://www.edenai.co/privacy-policy

Would you be open to a first class Eden AI provider under the partnership exception? If you would rather we stay on the Generic OpenAI connector, that is totally fine too, and we would be happy to contribute a short docs how to so EU users can find it easily. Glad to chat on Discord or by email, whatever is easiest for you.

Thanks a lot.

title: [FEAT]: AnythingLLM's Generic OpenAI allow passthrough of user-defined req params
body:
### How are you running AnythingLLM?

Docker (local)

### What happened?

## AnythingLLM's Generic OpenAI provider silently drops all sampling params except `temperature`

**Type:** Feature request (arguably a bug, given it silently ignores standard OpenAI Chat Completions fields)

**Version:** 1.15.0 (server), Generic OpenAI (`generic-openai`) provider

### Summary

`GenericOpenAiLLM` (`server/utils/AiProviders/genericOpenAi/index.js`) hardcodes the request body sent to the configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint to exactly four fields - `model`, `messages`, `temperature`, `max_tokens` (plus `stream_options` when `GENERIC_OPEN_AI_REPORT_USAGE=true`). Every other standard OpenAI Chat Completions parameter - `top_p`, `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty`, `seed`, `stop`, and any provider-specific extensions such as `repetition_penalty` - is dropped, with no config surface (env var, workspace setting, or otherwise) to set them.

```js
// getChatCompletion(), current behavior
this.openai.chat.completions.create({
  model: this.model,
  messages,
  temperature,
  max_tokens: this.maxTokens,
})

// streamGetChatCompletion(), same gap
this.openai.chat.completions.create({
  model: this.model,
  stream: true,
  messages,
  temperature,
  max_tokens: this.maxTokens,
  ...this.#includeStreamOptionsUsage(),
})
```

Since this already goes through the official `openai` npm SDK's `.chat.completions.create()`, adding more fields to these object literals is all that's required on the SDK side - the client will happily forward whatever is set.

### Why it matters

This provider is the primary integration point for self-hosted / local OpenAI-compatible inference servers (llama.cpp, vLLM, LM Studio, MLX-based servers, etc.). These are exactly the deployments most likely to need `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty`, or a `repetition_penalty`-style parameter, because smaller/quantized local models degrade into repetition loops far more often than hosted frontier models. Today, the only way to set any such setting is via the *inference server's own* global default (if it exposes one) - there's no way to set it per-workspace, per-request, or even at all if the server doesn't have its own global sampling config. A batch/automation workspace running a bulk generation task and an interactive chat workspace are forced to share identical sampling behavior with no override path.

Concretely: we run a local quantized Gemma-4 behind an OpenAI-compatible server that does support `repetition_penalty`, `presence_penalty`, and `frequency_penalty` per-request - but because AnythingLLM's generic-openai provider never sends them, they're unreachable from any AnythingLLM workspace. We ended up bypassing AnythingLLM's chat API entirely for one automation job and calling our inference server directly just to set these - which works, but throws away RAG/workspace context management that would otherwise be useful for that job.

### Suggested fix

Two options, not mutually exclusive:

1. **Minimal / targeted:** support the standard OpenAI fields already part of the Chat Completions spec - `top_p`, `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty`, `seed`, `stop` - via new env vars following the existing `GENERIC_OPEN_AI_*` convention (e.g. `GENERIC_OPEN_AI_TOP_P`, `GENERIC_OPEN_AI_FREQUENCY_PENALTY`, `GENERIC_OPEN_AI_PRESENCE_PENALTY`), only including each in the request object if set (so servers that reject unknown fields aren't broken by defaults).

2. **General escape hatch:** a single `GENERIC_OPEN_AI_EXTRA_PARAMS` env var (JSON object, merged into the request body before the API call) so provider-specific/non-standard fields - e.g. some local servers' `repetition_penalty`, or XTC-style anti-repetition sampling (`xtc_probability`/`xtc_threshold`) - can be set without AnythingLLM needing to special-case every inference server's extensions. This is lower-effort to implement and covers the long tail of server-specific params option (1) can't anticipate.

Happy to test a patch against our setup if that's useful, or provide more detail on our specific server's OpenAPI schema for the extra params it exposes.

title: [FEAT]: Add the option to set max_tokens in Together AI config
body:
### What would you like to see?

Currently, when using Together AI, there is no way to set `max_tokens`. Together AI's default for `max_tokens` is 2048. This typically results in truncation of the responses, which **makes Together AI essentially unusable with thinking models** (and, if you use the application specifically in the described scenario, as I do, unusable altogether).

It is possible to register Together AI as a "Generic OpenAI" provider. One can then use the UI to set `max_tokens` to the desired value and thus prevent truncation, but the functionality gets severely degraded (fetching the model list does not work so no way to select the model in chat; also no way to see the thinking trace).

I feel the best way to address this would be to expose `max_tokens` in the Together AI's config UI in the same way it's exposed for Generic OpenAI.

This issue is essentially #1945 but I'm describing it here because it's much more severe specifically for Together AI (and, possibly, some other providers too).

#6048 is related - it may or may not be a part of the solution.
